verdict.line: You lose if you let Mini Gnar sit at max range chucking Boulder/Boomerang Throw for free while his Rage fills uncontested; you win if you close with Q (Lunge), punish his auto-attacks with W (Riposte), and force skirmishes before he gets a comfortable Mega Gnar transform.

brief.thesis: Gnar's entire threat profile flips depending on his Rage bar: Mini Gnar is a squishy ranged poker who wants distance and E (Hop) escapes, while Mega Gnar is a melee bruiser with a stun and an AoE slam. Fiora's job is to deny Mini Gnar his comfortable range with Q (Lunge) and punish his auto-attack pokes with W (Riposte), so he either loses the trade outright or burns Rage into a Mega transform that still can't out-sustain her Duelist healing.

theirWindow.what: Back off immediately. Mega Gnar's W (Wallop) is a stun in the area in front of him and his E (Crunch) smashes down around him on landing — both hit area, not single-target, so don't stand close just because you dodged one. Respect that his R (GNAR!) throws enemies in a chosen direction and stuns anyone it hits into a wall, so never fight with your back to terrain once it's off cooldown.

yourWindow.what: Close the gap with Q (Lunge) rather than trading pokes at range — his Boomerang Throw outranges your dash (1100 vs 600), so sitting back just lets him farm free damage. Hold W (Riposte) for the moment he commits to an auto-attack trade; it parries his next basic attack and reflects magic damage back, which Boomerang Throw itself won't trigger since it's a spell, not an auto.

start.why: Pairs with Duelist's stacking heal to let you actually contest Mini Gnar's poke in extended trades instead of just losing the HP war.

boots.why: Gnar's damage is almost entirely physical — ranged autos, W (Hyper) empowered attacks, and Mega Gnar's melee combo — so flat armor mitigates more than anything Mercury's Treads offers here.

core.why: AoE sustain and wave pressure punish Mini Gnar's low HP pool and let Duelist stacks pile up fast in skirmishes.
The move speed proc stacks with E (Burst of Speed)'s on-hit move speed, which is exactly what you need to stick to Mega Gnar when he tries to Hop or Crunch away.
Damage-over-time mitigation plus healing lets you survive a Mega Gnar W (Wallop) stun into E (Crunch) combo and keep fighting through it instead of dying to the burst window.

situational.when: you are ahead and want a harder all-in burst window with the damage shield proc
you are already committed to the Hydra sustain path and want more raw damage in extended fights
the enemy team is stacking magic damage and you need the spell shield to survive

runes.keystoneWhy: Rewards the sustained auto-attack strings you're forcing by closing distance on Mini Gnar — the vulnerability proc squeezes extra damage out of exactly the extended skirmishes this matchup is won in.

summoners.why: Ignite converts the matchup's measured solo-kill advantage into actual kills during your all-in windows, and Flash gives you a way to reposition around Boomerang Throw or dodge the wall-stun angle on Mega Gnar's R (GNAR!).

playing.title: Close distance, don't poke-trade
playing.detail: Sitting at range just lets Mini Gnar land free Boomerang Throws since it outranges your Lunge. Walk up and threaten Q (Lunge) on cooldown instead.

playing.title: Save Riposte for his auto, not his Q
playing.detail: W (Riposte) only parries basic attacks, so it won't catch Boomerang Throw. Time it for when he's forced to auto-attack you in melee range.

playing.title: Track Rage, disengage before the transform
playing.detail: Once his Rage bar is near max, back off a step before he transforms — Mega Gnar's W (Wallop) stun and E (Crunch) slam both hit areas around him, not just where you were standing.

playing.title: Punish the long Q cooldown
playing.detail: Boomerang Throw sits at 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s and only refreshes faster if he catches it. If he whiffs or doesn't catch it, that's your all-in window with Lunge's free second dash.

playing.title: Never fight with your back to a wall
playing.detail: Once his R (GNAR!) is available — and it hits 0 cooldown at max rank — getting thrown into terrain adds a stun and bonus damage on top of the knockback.

playing.title: Chase Mega Gnar with stacked Burst of Speed
playing.detail: Landing autos or Lunges during E (Burst of Speed) stacks move speed, which is how you stay on top of him when he tries to Hop or Crunch away to reset.

playing.title: Look for the kill after he commits a cooldown
playing.detail: The matchup's measured solo-kill edge is real — after he throws Boomerang Throw or Hops without a target, that's the window to all-in with Ignite up.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, rune pages, and all win-rate/pick-rate numbers above are pulled from measured OP.GG games on the current patch (16.19.1); the ability breakdowns, timing windows, and tactical reasoning are my own read on why those numbers come out the way they do.

stats.opponentTip: Be careful of Mega Gnar’s (R) at all times. Do not let Mini Gnar punish you by keeping your distance when contesting lane.
